**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no exclusivity obligation binding Sparkling, which satisfies the rule's **preferred** position rather than merely the fallback — so there is nothing to narrow or delete.

What I checked:
- **§2 Grant of License** — licence is expressly "non-transferable and non-exclusive"; no reciprocal commitment by us to source only from Garman.
- **§3 Restrictions on Use** — standard licence limitations (no copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing, and a duty to prevent third-party misuse). None restricts our ability to buy competing products or retain third-party maintainers.
- **§10 Maintenance and Support** — Garman's obligations run to us; no clause makes Garman our sole source of maintenance, updates or support.
- **§11 Fees, §19 Non-Solicitation, §20 General Matters** and boilerplate — no minimum-purchase or requirements commitment.
- Targeted searches for "exclusive", "sole", "requirements from", "procure", "supplier", "competitor", "third party" surfaced only benign or customer-favourable uses: non-exclusive escrow licence (p0115), mutual exclusive-remedy provision (p0105), and non-exclusive jurisdiction (p0146).

Per the detection guidance, the non-exclusive licence and non-exclusive jurisdiction language is not a deviation, and the mutual exclusive-remedy clause in §15 is a liability term that belongs to the limitation-of-liability rule, not this one — I deliberately did not flag it here to avoid double-counting the same commercial term. We retain full freedom to procure from other suppliers.
